neighbours.label: prior expectations or assumed knowledge brought to a situation (preconceived notions, certain expectations, assume they already know), versus the same frames about objects or actions
fire: Good researchers try to approach each case without preconceived notions.
She came to the new job with certain expectations about the hours.
Readers often bring preconceived ideas about the author to the book.
Too many managers assume they already know what customers want.
We entered the old house without any expectations, and it charmed us.
Jurors must set aside preconceived opinions about the defendant.
The guide assumes the reader already knows how to use a compass.
Travelers with preconceived images of the city are often surprised.
quiet: Good researchers try to keep careful records of each case.
She arrived at the new job carrying a laptop and a lunch box.
Readers often bring their own bookmarks to the library.
Too many managers work late on Fridays.
We entered the old house through the back door, and it charmed us.
Jurors must sit quietly while the witness speaks.
The guide shows the reader how to use a compass.
Travelers with heavy suitcases are often tired by noon.
